h: Make the most of your Arndale session
p: A little planning makes a big difference here. Because the Gamebox is inside the Arndale, it's tempting to do your shopping first, but leaving the bags with someone who isn't playing is a much better plan. You'll be moving quickly and you won't want anything underfoot. Trainers and comfortable clothes are best, and listening carefully to the briefing at the start will save you a lot of frantic flailing later.

Sessions run for a set time, and the game choices change from time to time, so see what's on when booking. Pick something that suits your group: gentler themes for families with younger children, and faster, more competitive games for teens and adults. Divide up jobs once you're in, as teamwork beats raw button-mashing every time.

For a breather afterwards, the Arndale's food market is a handy place to grab something to eat, with plenty of different cuisines under one roof. Or step outside and wander over to Exchange Square and the area around the Cathedral, both just a minute or two away.

Manchester also has plenty of culture close by if you want to extend the day. The Royal Exchange Theatre, inside the grand former cotton exchange on St Ann's Square, is famous for its theatre-in-the-round, and Chetham's Library, near the cathedral, is a historic library dating back to the 1650s. Great places to combine with an hour of frantic gaming. Victoria station is only a few minutes' walk away, so getting home afterwards is easy too.
